records.label: tail wag joy cue
records.visual_function: Use a big, fast, sweeping tail wag as the visible proof of happiness or high positive arousal in tailed anthro characters.
records.prompt: Show a large fast sweeping tail wag with loose body follow-through: the tail base moves with the character, the wag amplitude is wide, and the ears and face carry matching open happiness.
invariants: wag amplitude scales with the strength of the joy
the tail and the facial expression support the same positive emotion
the body stays loose and the tail follows through from the base during a joy wag
misreadings_to_avoid: a stiff or slow tail read as joy
tail motion copied onto a stubby-tailed lineage such as bear characters
a tail wag pasted on while the face stays neutral or flat

search_terms.phrase: big fast tail wag for happiness

records.label: tail small sway anticipation cue
records.visual_function: Use a small, slow, hesitant tail sway as the visible marker of excited expectation or focused attention.
records.prompt: Show a small low-amplitude tail sway, often with the body leaning slightly forward, ears oriented toward the object of attention, and eyes fixed on it.
invariants: sway amplitude stays small and slow compared with a joy wag
the gaze, ear orientation, and tail sway point at the same expected thing
the body holds a forward-leaning ready stance while the sway stays low and slow
misreadings_to_avoid: the small sway read as boredom or indifference
sway so wide it reads as a joy wag
the small sway paired with a slack, disengaged face

search_terms.phrase: small slow tail sway while expecting something

records.label: tail droop sadness cue
records.visual_function: Use a drooping, lowered tail as the visible marker of sadness, deflation, or shame in tailed anthro characters.
records.prompt: Show the tail hanging low and still, with lowered ears, rounded shoulders, a downcast gaze, and slack arms so the whole silhouette deflates together into one settled, heavy shape.
invariants: the tail hangs low and holds mostly still
the ears, posture, and gaze agree with the drooping tail
the spine and shoulders round downward so the whole silhouette settles with the tail
misreadings_to_avoid: a drooping tail combined with a bright open grin
tail droop used on lineages whose tails cannot emote, such as bear or elephant characters
a lowered tail that still carries a wide, fast sweep

search_terms.phrase: low still tail with downcast mood

records.label: tail stiff alert cue
records.visual_function: Use a stiff, rigid, bristled tail as the visible marker of alertness, fear, or a threat read in tailed anthro characters.
records.prompt: Show the tail held rigid, either straight out or raised and puffed, with wide eyes, pinned or rotated alert ears, and weight shifted back onto the legs.
invariants: the tail reads rigid and locked along its whole length
the ears, eyes, and weight shift agree with the threat or alarm read
the fur or scales along the tail lift so the silhouette widens under alarm
misreadings_to_avoid: the rigid tail read as relaxed confidence
bristling combined with a soft happy face
a bristled tail on a lineage whose tail carries little fur

search_terms.phrase: puffed rigid tail with wide eyes

records.label: feline tail up purr contentment cue
records.visual_function: Use an upright, gently quivering tail plus a purring, softened face as the feline-lineage visible marker of calm contentment.
records.prompt: Show the tail held upright with a slight quiver at the tip, relaxed half-lidded or softly closed eyes, a still or kneading posture, and a calm reserved mouth that still reads as pleased.
invariants: the upright tail reads as settled contentment
the face stays calm and reserved so contentment shows through soft eyes and easy posture
the tip quiver stays small so the upright tail keeps its relaxed line
misreadings_to_avoid: the upright tail read as the canine joy wag
a wide open grin pasted onto a calm feline face
a rigid upright tail held stiff enough to read as alarm

search_terms.phrase: feline tail up purr contentment cue
upright quivering tail with purring calm face

records.label: rabbit nose twitch stress cue
records.visual_function: Use a rapid nose twitch as the lagomorph-lineage visible marker of stress, irritation, or suppressed anger.
records.prompt: Show the small split nose twitching rapidly and repeatedly across several beats, combined with flattened or backward-angled ears, a tense jaw, and stiffened shoulders that hold the irritation.
invariants: the twitch repeats rapidly across several beats
the ear angle agrees with the stressed or angry read
the shoulders and jaw hold tension that matches the twitch rate
misreadings_to_avoid: the nose twitch read as a casual sniffing gesture
a calm face with a rapid angry twitch
a slow, single nose movement standing in for the rapid twitch

search_terms.phrase: rapid nose twitch while stressed or angry

records.label: avian feather fluff alarm cue
records.visual_function: Use a sudden body-wide feather fluff as the avian-lineage visible marker of alarm or startle.
records.prompt: Show the feather coat lifting and fluffing out across the body and wings for a beat, with wide eyes and a recoiling or freezing posture.
invariants: the fluff reads as a volume change across the whole feather coat
the posture and eyes agree with the startle read
the fluff lasts a beat and then settles back into the sleek coat
misreadings_to_avoid: fluffed feathers read as casual preening or comfort
fluffing used on non-feathered lineages
a slow gradual puff that loses the suddenness of the startle

records.label: fluke wag happiness cue
records.visual_function: Use side-to-side fluke wagging as the marine-lineage visible marker of happiness or excitement in orca and shark anthro characters.
records.prompt: Show the two-fluke tail wagging side to side with visible motion lines or water splash, paired with an eager forward lean and bright eyes.
invariants: the paired flukes move together as one tail fin
the excitement read is shared by the posture and face
the wag drives from the tail stock so the whole body carries the motion
misreadings_to_avoid: the fluke wag drawn as a mammalian furry tail wag
a fluke wag on non-marine lineages
flukes drawn as two separate legs or limbs

search_terms.phrase: orca or shark fluke wagging with excitement

records.label: heavy tail thump emphasis cue
records.visual_function: Use a single hard tail thump against the floor or a surface as the dragon and reptilian-lineage visible marker of emphasis, irritation, or rising excitement.
records.prompt: Show the big heavy tail raised and struck down once against the ground with an impact read: dust, a small bounce of nearby objects, or a sharp motion line, paired with a tensed stance.
invariants: the thump lands as a single strike or a slow deliberate beat
the face and stance carry the matching irritation or emphasis
the tail mass and thickness make the impact believable
misreadings_to_avoid: the thump read as a playful wag
a light flexible tail that could not produce an impact
a rapid drumming that loses the weight of a single strike

search_terms.phrase: heavy tail strike on the ground
